title: SDK Sprint Factory: Initiative and OKR Syncboard
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a repeatable, measurable ‘Sprint Factory’ for Developer Experience that churns SDKs, docs, and quickstarts on a predictable cadence. The goal is to reduce time-to-publish for SDK integrations from idea -> published quickstart from 6 weeks to 2 weeks for high-priority languages, while tracking OKRs that connect to activation and retention metrics. This ticket coordinates cross-functional work: PM playbooks, design patterns, engineering templates, CI/CD automation, and an observability dashboard for initiative-level KPIs.
acceptance_criteria: A documented Sprint Factory playbook exists (Confluence) describing roles, cadence, and handoff artifacts
Two language SDK quickstarts published through the new pipeline within the cycle and validated against activation metric targets
Automated CI checks that validate example app builds and smoke tests are added to the SDK template repository
A dashboard that surfaces SDK quickstart activation (first successful API call), time-to-first-hello, and retention metrics is live
OKR mapping is attached: O1/O2 alignment with owners and measurable targets for Cycle 2025-W06

Design: Create quickstart template components and copy style guide (Figma: /figma/redwood/dx-quickstart-templates)
Eng: Implement SDK template repo with CI pipeline and smoke test harness (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-templates/pull/247)
Eng: Wire telemetry hooks for activation and retention into dx-metrics pipeline (dashboard link below)
PM/Eng: Run two pilot sprints for Go and Ruby and collect time-to-publish and activation signals

decisions: Adopt an opinionated quickstart structure: intro, minimal sample app, smoke test, telemetry snippet. Keeps variance low across languages.
Two-week sprint cadence for pilots, then graduate successful recipe to a biweekly production Sprint Factory.
Prioritize languages by webhook activity and signups: initial pilots = Go, Ruby. Next wave: Python, JavaScript.
risks: CI infra for ephemeral keys might delay pipeline by 1 sprint if security approvals take longer than expected.
If design patterns are too rigid across languages, SDK owners may reject templates causing rework.
Telemetry gaps could make activation metrics noisy; need strict event contracts from engineering.
next_steps: Complete infra dependency ticket for ephemeral test keys (ENG-48123) and confirm timeline
Run Ruby pilot and capture activation/retention signals; retrofit any CI flakiness
Finalize Sprint Factory playbook and run a 30-minute enablement session for SDK owners (calendar invite sent)
Add OKR targets to central tracker and notify GTM/analytics owners for KPI wiring
